accepted.reason: Observation-target alignment is good: hospitalization admissions plausibly lag an incidence proxy, and a short (1-week) delay is a reasonable single-axis perturbation around the currently discovered 2–3 week delayed_I patterns. Complexity is unchanged (no added compartments, no fractional memory), so overfitting risk stays low for n_train=31. Identifiability is comparable to the existing best templates and avoids introducing an explicit H compartment, which is noted as weakly identifiable in short single-season data.

SEIR + delayed_I(2w) remains well-aligned with hospitalization-rate semantics via the delay and is simpler than SEIRS, which can reduce over-flexibility in a 31-week window. Identifiability is improved relative to SEIRS because waning (S↔R) can be weakly informed in single-season data. Main risk is underfitting if within-season waning/replenishment is actually needed to match tail/late-season curvature, but it is still a reasonable parsimonious comparator.

SEIRS with direct I observation is a parsimonious baseline and can help test whether this age group’s hospitalization-rate series is effectively contemporaneous with the I proxy. However, it is less plausible mechanistically than delayed_I for admissions data and is likely to be phase-advanced around turning points, so it is lower priority than delayed mappings.

suggested_edits.edit: If allowed within the same structure family, consider changing observation_map from "I" to "delayed_I" with delay_weeks=0 (explicitly encoding the no-lag hypothesis while keeping the hospitalization-oriented observation family). If not allowed, keep as-is but note it is primarily a diagnostic baseline for phase alignment rather than a likely best template.
